label: D2: reached S1 via common a1, after a rewarded or S1 previous trial
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and only when the input shows action a1 and state S1, i.e. a common a1->S1 transition (never on S2, a2, or rare a1->S2 / a2->S1). Within those steps it is gated by the recent history: it fires when the previous trial was rewarded or the previous trial also reached S1 (dev F1 0.94, mass recall 0.99). The bare a1->S1-common predicate has recall 1.0 but precision 0.69. Magnitude builds over runs of consecutive rewarded common a1->S1 trials (it climbs toward the max across the window, e.g. 0.4 -> 0.7 -> 0.9 -> 1.0) and is weak after an unrewarded or S2 trial. It also correlates with high value (top value bin holds 53% of the mass). Most of the remaining misses are weak activations on the first trial of a window, where the previous trial is unknown. All variables used are observed at D2, so no future information is needed. Reads as an S1-is-good / stay-on-a1 evidence accumulator at D2.

issues: The 'rewarded OR S1 previous trial' clause is wrong. The feature never fires after a rewarded S2 previous trial: the predicate B & prev_reward==1 & prev_state==2, with B = D2 & a1 & S1, has precision 0.000 over 4870 predicted steps (dev). This is one systematic class, and it accounts for about half of the original predicate's 9706 dev false positives.

What actually matters is that the previous trial reached S1, ideally rewarded. After a rewarded S1 trial it fires at precision 0.994 (recall 0.676), whether the previous trial got there by a1 (0.996) or by a rare a2 transition (0.971). After an unrewarded S1 trial it fires at only 0.652 precision, and that depends on the trial two back: it fires at 0.866 if that trial was a rewarded S1, 0.078 if it was an unrewarded S1, and 0.000 if it was S2. After an unrewarded S2 trial it is essentially silent (0.0016).

The prev_reward==1 disjunct only helps on the window's first trial, where prev_state is unknown (-1). There B & prev_state==-1 & prev_reward==1 has precision 0.972 and covers about 22% of activations. So the disjunct works by standing in for an unseen S1 trial, not because any rewarded trial is enough.

Minor: 'never fires on a2 or rare transitions' is almost true but not exactly. On dev there are 69 activations on rare a2->S1 at D2, which is negligible mass. The claims that the feature is D2-only (100% of mass) and never fires on S2 were confirmed.
The original predicate's test scores reproduce: precision 0.893, recall 0.98, F1 0.935, mass recall 0.988. But its false positives are systematic, not scattered noise.
skeptic.revised_label: D2: reached S1 via common a1, when the recent history (prev trial and, if it was unrewarded, the one before) shows rewarded S1 outcomes and no S2 visit; silent after any S2 previous trial
